stations.title: Refuge from exile
stations.text: The Trappists of Mont des Cats in northern France feared being expelled from France and sought refuge abroad. Abbot Dominique Lacaes sent the former Zouave officer Sébastien Wyart to find a place in England or the Netherlands.

stations.title: Founding at Berkel-Enschot
stations.text: In March 1881 Mont des Cats founded Koningshoeven Monastery near Tilburg. The site was the Schaapskooi, a group of farmsteads that the Dutch Crown Prince Willem had had built in 1834.

stations.title: Raised to a priory
stations.text: According to the Cistercian Order (OCSO), the young community was raised to a priory in 1883. Farming alone could not yet support the monastery.

stations.title: The brewery is established
stations.text: In 1884 the monks set up a brewery within the monastery walls to fund the monastery and its charitable work. The beer is still sold under the name La Trappe today.

stations.title: Koningshoeven becomes an abbey
stations.text: According to the OCSO, the community was raised to an abbey in 1891. Dom Willibrord Verbruggen is regarded as its first abbot.

stations.title: Dispute over the Trappist seal
stations.text: In 1999 the abbey signed a contract with the brewing group Bavaria, which took over the running of the brewery. As a result Koningshoeven lost the right to call its beer a Trappist beer.

stations.title: The seal returns
stations.text: Following an application of February 2005, the International Trappist Association allowed the brewery to use the official Trappist logo again. The brewery continues to be run by a Bavaria subsidiary, while the abbey retains the buildings and oversight.
